# Clunking noise when braking -- possibly bad CV axle?

A clanking sound that appears specifically during right-hand turns, coupled with a vibrating steering wheel, points to a mechanical failure rather than an electrical glitch or software bug. In your 2007 Sienna XLE V6, the symptoms you describeâstarting with a persistent issue after a boot replacement and evolving into intermittent noise and loosenessâsuggest that the initial repair may have been incomplete or that secondary damage occurred during the service event.

The most probable culprit is indeed the CV axle assembly, but the diagnosis requires distinguishing between the outer joint (which was addressed by the boot replacement) and the inner joint or the center splines. When you replace a CV boot, you are essentially swapping a protective sleeve for grease; if the lip of the old boot was torn or if the seal wasn't perfect during installation, contamination can enter quickly. However, the specific symptom of a "clank" when turning right indicates that a bearing surface is collapsing or that the axle shaft has slipped out of proper alignment.

Consider the mechanics of the Constant Velocity joint. It relies on a precise balance of grease and tight tolerances to handle torque loads in all directions. A clunk upon braking while turning right suggests that the load vector is shifting abruptly. When you brake, weight transfers forward; when you turn right, the lateral force pushes against the left-side suspension components. If the CV joint has excessive play or if the bearing races are worn, the shaft may momentarily disengage from its optimal path before settling back, creating that metallic impact noise. This is distinct from a U-joint clunk, which typically happens in rear-wheel-drive vehicles due to driveshaft angle changes, whereas your Sienna is front-wheel drive.

The fact that the noise stopped occasionally and then returned intermittently is a classic sign of worn bearings or loose retaining clips inside the joint. Think of it like a mechanical switch that is failing to stay latched. The vibration in the steering wheel confirms that the issue is transmitting through the suspension geometry directly to the rack and pinion. A loose steering feel further corroborates this, as play in the axle often mimics looseness in the steering linkage because the driver feels the gap closing and opening under load.

It is also possible that the initial boot replacement damaged the inner seal or that the outer joint failed immediately after due to improper grease filling. Some technicians might assume a new boot guarantees a new seal, but if the lip wasn't seated correctly on the shaft groove, the seal fails regardless of how fresh the grease looks. This can lead to rapid wear on the ball bearings within the joint, causing the "clank" you hear when the load shifts during braking and turning.

Given the progression from constant noise to intermittent behavior, the internal components are likely deteriorating. Waiting for it to stop completely is risky, as a catastrophic failure of an inner CV joint can result in the axle shaft separating entirely while driving, leading to a loss of power to that wheel. The trade-off here is between immediate safety and waiting for the car to be completely unusable. Since the steering is already feeling loose, the play has likely exceeded safe operating limits.

If you are considering repair options, replacing just the boot again is not a viable solution; the joint itself needs to be inspected for bearing wear and spline integrity. In many cases, replacing the entire CV axle assembly is more cost-effective than trying to salvage a joint that has already exhibited clunking behavior. Ensure that any replacement part matches the exact specifications of your 2007 Sienna V6, as variations in spline count or diameter can alter drivetrain dynamics.
